title: Add torrenttrackerslist.com under Third-party online tools
body:
Hi @ngosang — long-time consumer of your list here, thanks for keeping it
maintained.

This PR adds one line under **Third-party online tools** for
https://www.torrenttrackerslist.com — a web UI that:

- pulls `trackers_all.txt` from this repo as upstream truth (credited on-site)
- lets a user paste the trackers already in their `.torrent` / magnet and
  reports live up/down + round-trip latency per tracker
- offers one-click copy formatted for qBittorrent, µTorrent and Deluge

It complements the repo rather than replacing it — people who want the raw
.txt still come here; people who want "is tracker X up right now?" get an
answer without spinning up their own checker.

Happy to tweak the wording, move it to a different section, or close this if
you'd rather not list web frontends. No hard feelings either way — and
thanks again for the list.

title: {Not A Bug} End User Tracker Checker [Python Script & Compiled Windows .exe}
body:
Just sharing in case its useful to anyone else...

I sometimes int he past have grabbed tracker lists form multiple sources, some a downlaoded txt file, some added via URL to a torrent client, but i really dont enjoy long lists of non-working trackers being added/re-annoucned and im a tidy freak, so i wrote this 

It:

- reads in a text file or URL containing torrent trackers
- parses out any lines NOT beginning with udp://, http:// or https://
- sorts and uniqs the results
- tests each tracker for existence/connectivity, timeout and retry values adjustable
- removes all that fail to a failed.txt file
- writes the working ones to a working.txt file (id rather add known working ones to my torrent client manually)
- writes just the domains to a allow_domain.txt file (i run a domain blocking list on dnscrypt-proxy)

command line arguments (not all are required, some have defaults):

filename - local filemane (no --file prefix required)
--url (URL to trackerlist, no default)
--workers (number of worker threads, default: 20)
--timeout (timeout value per tracker, default: 5)
--retries (number of retries per tracker, default: 2)

Code:

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
check_trackers.py - Filter, deduplicate, and test torrent tracker URLs.

Usage:
    python check_trackers.py [input_file] [--url URL] [--timeout 5] [--workers 20] [--retries 2]

    At least one of input_file or --url must be supplied. Both can be used together
    and their tracker lists will be merged, deduplicated, and tested as one set.

Examples:
    python check_trackers.py trackers.txt
    python check_trackers.py --url https://example.com/trackers.txt
    python check_trackers.py trackers.txt --url https://example.com/trackers.txt

Outputs:
    working.txt         - Trackers that responded successfully
    failed.txt          - Trackers that failed all attempts
    allowed_domains.txt - Bare hostnames from working trackers (no IPs)
"""

import sys
import socket
import struct
import random
import argparse
import threading
from urllib.parse import urlparse
from urllib.request import urlopen, Request
from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

VALID_PREFIXES = ("udp://", "http://", "https://")


# ---------- Loading ----------------------------------------------------------

def lines_from_file(path):
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return f.readlines()


def lines_from_url(url):
    print("  Fetching URL: %s" % url)
    try:
        req = Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "tracker-checker/1.0"})
        with urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:
            return resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(keepends=True)
    except Exception as e:
        print("  ERROR fetching URL: %s" % e)
        sys.exit(1)


def filter_lines(lines):
    return [
        line.strip()
        for line in lines
        if line.strip().startswith(VALID_PREFIXES)
    ]


def load_and_filter(file_path, url):
    """
    Load lines from a local file and/or a remote URL, merge them,
    filter to valid-prefix lines, then sort and deduplicate.
    """
    all_lines = []

    if file_path:
        file_lines = lines_from_file(file_path)
        print("  File lines  : %d  (%s)" % (len(file_lines), file_path))
        all_lines.extend(file_lines)

    if url:
        url_lines = lines_from_url(url)
        print("  URL lines   : %d  (%s)" % (len(url_lines), url))
        all_lines.extend(url_lines)

    filtered = filter_lines(all_lines)
    unique_sorted = sorted(set(filtered))

    print("  ----------")
    print("  Total raw   : %d lines" % len(all_lines))
    print("  After filter: %d valid-prefix lines" % len(filtered))
    print("  After dedup : %d unique trackers" % len(unique_sorted))
    return unique_sorted


# ---------- Connectivity tests -----------------------------------------------

def test_udp(host, port, timeout):
    """Send a minimal UDP tracker connect-request packet and wait for a reply."""
    transaction_id = random.randint(0, 0xFFFFFFFF)
    packet = struct.pack(">QII", 0x41727101980, 0, transaction_id)
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
        sock.settimeout(timeout)
        sock.sendto(packet, (host, port))
        data, _ = sock.recvfrom(16)
        sock.close()
        return len(data) >= 8
    except Exception:
        return False


def test_http(url, timeout):
    """
    Probe the tracker's /announce endpoint.
    Many trackers return 400 Bad Request for a bare GET - that still means
    the server is alive, so any HTTP-level response counts as reachable.
    Only a network-level failure counts as unreachable.
    """
    try:
        probe = url if "/announce" in url else url.rstrip("/") + "/announce"
        req = urlopen(probe, timeout=timeout)
        req.close()
        return True
    except HTTPError:
        return True   # Got an HTTP reply - server is alive
    except URLError as e:
        reason = str(e.reason) if hasattr(e, "reason") else str(e)
        if "Connection refused" in reason or "actively refused" in reason:
            return True
        return False
    except Exception:
        return False


def test_tracker(url, timeout, retries):
    """
    Test a tracker up to (1 + retries) times. A single success is enough
    to mark it working - only fail if every attempt fails.
    """
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    scheme = parsed.scheme.lower()
    host   = parsed.hostname or ""
    port   = parsed.port

    if not host:
        return url, False

    for _ in range(1 + retries):
        if scheme == "udp":
            ok = test_udp(host, port or 80, timeout)
        else:
            ok = test_http(url, timeout)
        if ok:
            return url, True   # pass on any successful attempt

    return url, False          # failed every attempt


# ---------- Domain extraction ------------------------------------------------

def extract_domain(url):
    """Return the bare hostname from a tracker URL, e.g.:
        udp://tracker.example.com:6969/announce  ->  tracker.example.com
        https://tracker.example.com/announce     ->  tracker.example.com
    """
    return (urlparse(url).hostname or "").lower()


def is_ip_address(host):
    """Return True if host is an IPv4 or IPv6 address rather than a hostname."""
    for family in (socket.AF_INET, socket.AF_INET6):
        try:
            socket.inet_pton(family, host)
            return True
        except (socket.error, OSError):
            pass
    return False


def write_allowed_domains(working_urls, path="allowed_domains.txt"):
    domains = sorted(set(
        d for d in (extract_domain(u) for u in working_urls)
        if d and not is_ip_address(d)
    ))
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(domains) + ("\n" if domains else ""))
    return domains


# ---------- Main -------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Filter and test torrent trackers from a file and/or URL.",
        epilog="At least one of input_file or --url must be provided."
    )
    parser.add_argument("input_file", nargs="?", default=None,
                        help="Path to a local tracker list file (optional)")
    parser.add_argument("--url",      default=None,
                        help="URL to fetch an additional tracker list from")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout",  type=float, default=5,
                        help="Seconds to wait per attempt (default: 5)")
    parser.add_argument("--workers",  type=int,   default=20,
                        help="Parallel workers (default: 20)")
    parser.add_argument("--retries",  type=int,   default=2,
                        help="Extra attempts before marking a tracker failed (default: 2)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not args.input_file and not args.url:
        parser.error("Provide at least one of: input_file or --url")

    print("\n-- Step 1: Load & filter --")
    trackers = load_and_filter(args.input_file, args.url)

    if not trackers:
        print("No valid trackers found. Exiting.")
        sys.exit(0)

    print("\n-- Step 2: Testing %d trackers "
          "(timeout=%.1fs, retries=%d, workers=%d) --"
          % (len(trackers), args.timeout, args.retries, args.workers))

    working, failed = [], []
    lock = threading.Lock()
    done = [0]

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
        futures = {
            pool.submit(test_tracker, url, args.timeout, args.retries): url
            for url in trackers
        }
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            url, ok = future.result()
            with lock:
                done[0] += 1
                count = done[0]
            status = "OK  " if ok else "FAIL"
            print("  [%4d/%d] %s  %s" % (count, len(trackers), status, url))
            (working if ok else failed).append(url)

    working.sort()
    failed.sort()

    with open("working.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(working) + ("\n" if working else ""))

    with open("failed.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(failed) + ("\n" if failed else ""))

    print("\n-- Results --")
    print("  Working : %4d  -> working.txt" % len(working))
    print("  Failed  : %4d  -> failed.txt"  % len(failed))

    domains = write_allowed_domains(working)
    print("  Domains : %4d  -> allowed_domains.txt" % len(domains))
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


```

Obviously security prevents me form uploading/ttaching a compiled .exe, but it will compile via auto-py-to-exe as a one file, and has been tested via that method

title: Which list should the average user choose?
body:
Now that https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent/pull/21828 was merged, I am wondering which list I should use. It seems in the past (9 years ago!) you recommended using the UDP list if you don't have any issues with UDP trackers: https://github.com/ngosang/trackerslist/issues/7#issuecomment-225372496

Is this still the case, or should I use best / all / http / https instead?

Also, is there any reason to use best over all? There's obviously more bandwidth with all but other than that?
